flags.note: The flag misreads a disclosure as an omission: the quoted sentence IS the hindsight-bias disclosure. Section 2 expressly labels the figures hypothetical and supplies the C5 elements - criteria/assumptions (70/30 weights raised by the committee, monthly rebalancing, built from each composite's actual net-of-fee monthly returns), and risks/limitations (no account was ever managed as a 70/30 blend, no actual trading, no cost of moving assets at each rebalance, no cash flows, no committee decisions along the way, model composite fees of 0.32%/0.25% rather than the proposed fees, and an express warning that actual results would have differed, possibly materially, and could have been lower). It is also limited to the committee in light of the foundation's stated objectives, 4.5% spending policy and liquidity needs. The backtested-vs-forward-tested question is answered on the face of the text: historical composite returns with weights selected in 2026. Nothing further for a reviewer.

The quoted sentence is itself the balanced treatment - the income benefit and the offsetting interest rate risk appear in the same sentence ('but it carries more interest rate risk and will lose value when yields rise quickly'). The surrounding paragraph reinforces it: the preceding sentence quantifies the drawdown (calendar 2022, -11.4% net of fees, with the note that the five-year figure includes that year), the following sentence adds credit, liquidity and prepayment risk from corporate and securitized holdings relative to a Treasury-only portfolio, the hypothetical section discloses a -9.2% worst calendar year for the blend, and the footer repeats interest rate, credit, inflation, liquidity and prepayment risk plus 'value can fall as well as rise.' This is what C9 requires, so the text already carries it.
